approx_distinct.name: approx_distinct
approx_distinct.description: Returns the approximate number of distinct input values calculated using the HyperLogLog algorithm.

approx_median.name: approx_median
approx_median.description: Returns the approximate median (50th percentile) of input values. It is an alias of `approx_percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x)`.

approx_percentile_cont.name: approx_percentile_cont
approx_percentile_cont.description: Returns the approximate percentile of input values using the t-digest algorithm.
approx_percentile_cont.syntax: approx_percentile_cont(percentile [, centroids]) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY expression)
approx_percentile_cont.example: SELECT approx_percentile_cont(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY column_name) FROM table_name;

approx_percentile_cont_with_weight.name: approx_percentile_cont_with_weight
approx_percentile_cont_with_weight.description: Returns the weighted approximate percentile of input values using the t-digest algorithm.
approx_percentile_cont_with_weight.syntax: approx_percentile_cont_with_weight(weight, percentile [, centroids]) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY expression)
approx_percentile_cont_with_weight.example: SELECT approx_percentile_cont_with_weight(weight_column, 0.90) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY column_name) FROM table_name;

array_agg.name: array_agg
array_agg.description: Returns an array created from the expression elements. If ordering is required, elements are inserted in the specified order. This aggregation function can only mix DISTINCT and ORDER BY if the ordering expression is exactly the same as the argument expression.
array_agg.example: SELECT array_agg(column_name ORDER BY other_column) FROM table_name;

avg.name: avg
avg.description: Returns the average of numeric values in the specified column.

bit_and.name: bit_and
bit_and.description: Computes the bitwise AND of all non-null input values.

bit_or.name: bit_or
bit_or.description: Computes the bitwise OR of all non-null input values.

bit_xor.name: bit_xor
bit_xor.description: Computes the bitwise exclusive OR of all non-null input values.

bool_and.name: bool_and
bool_and.description: Returns true if all non-null input values are true, otherwise false.

bool_or.name: bool_or
bool_or.description: Returns true if all non-null input values are true, otherwise false.

count.name: count
count.description: Returns the number of non-null values in the specified column. To include null values in the total count, use `count(

first_value.name: first_value
first_value.description: Returns value evaluated at the row that is the first row of the window frame.
first_value.example:
SELECT department,
 employee_id,
 salary,
 first_value(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS top_salary
FROM employees;

grouping.name: grouping
grouping.description: Returns 1 if the data is aggregated across the specified column, or 0 if it is not aggregated in the result set.

last_value.name: last_value
last_value.description: Returns value evaluated at the row that is the last row of the window frame.
last_value.example:
SELECT department,
 employee_id,
 salary,
 last_value(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary) AS running_last_salary
FROM employees;

max.name: max
max.description: Returns the maximum value in the specified column.

median.name: median
median.description: Returns the median value in the specified column.

min.name: min
min.description: Returns the minimum value in the specified column.

percentile_cont.name: percentile_cont
percentile_cont.description: Returns the exact percentile of input values, interpolating between values if needed.
percentile_cont.example: SELECT percentile_cont(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY column_name) FROM table_name;

string_agg.name: string_agg
string_agg.description: Concatenates the values of string expressions and places separator values between them. If ordering is required, strings are concatenated in the specified order. This aggregation function can only mix DISTINCT and ORDER BY if the ordering expression is exactly the same as the first argument expression.
string_agg.example:
SELECT string_agg(name, ', ') AS names_list
 FROM employee;

sum.name: sum
sum.description: Returns the sum of all values in the specified column.

var.name: var
var.description: Returns the statistical sample variance of a set of numbers.

var_pop.name: var_pop
var_pop.description: Returns the statistical population variance of a set of numbers.

corr.name: corr
corr.description: Returns the coefficient of correlation between two numeric values.

covar_pop.name: covar_pop
covar_pop.description: Returns the sample covariance of a set of number pairs.

covar_samp.name: covar_samp
covar_samp.description: Returns the sample covariance of a set of number pairs.

nth_value.name: nth_value
nth_value.description: Returns the value evaluated at the nth row of the window frame (counting from 1). Returns NULL if no such row exists.

regr_avgx.name: regr_avgx
regr_avgx.description: Computes the average of the independent variable (input) expression_x for the non-null paired data points.

regr_avgy.name: regr_avgy
regr_avgy.description: Computes the average of the dependent variable (output) expression_y for the non-null paired data points.

regr_count.name: regr_count
regr_count.description: Counts the number of non-null paired data points.

regr_intercept.name: regr_intercept
regr_intercept.description: Computes the y-intercept of the linear regression line. For the equation (y = kx + b), this function returns b.

regr_r2.name: regr_r2
regr_r2.description: Computes the square of the correlation coefficient between the independent and dependent variables.

regr_slope.name: regr_slope
regr_slope.description: Returns the slope of the linear regression line for non-null pairs in aggregate columns. Given input column Y and X: regr_slope(Y, X) returns the slope (k in Y = k\

regr_sxx.name: regr_sxx
regr_sxx.description: Computes the sum of squares of the independent variable.

regr_sxy.name: regr_sxy
regr_sxy.description: Computes the sum of products of paired data points.

regr_syy.name: regr_syy
regr_syy.description: Computes the sum of squares of the dependent variable.

stddev.name: stddev
stddev.description: Returns the standard deviation of a set of numbers.

stddev_pop.name: stddev_pop
stddev_pop.description: Returns the population standard deviation of a set of numbers.

escaping.name: escaping
escaping.description: Unlike many other languages, SQL literals do not by default support C-style escape sequences such as `\n` for newline. Instead all characters in a `'` string are treated literally. To escape `'` in SQL literals, use `''`:

join.name: join
join.description: ```sql ( SELECT 'apples' AS item, 2 AS sales UNION ALL SELECT 'bananas' AS item, 5 AS sales ) |> AS produce_sales |> LEFT JOIN ( SELECT 'apples' AS item, 123 AS id ) AS produce_data ON produce_sales.item = produce_data.item |> SELECT produce_sales.item, sales, id; +--------+-------+------+ | item | sales | id | +--------+-------+------+ | apples | 2 | 123 | | bananas| 5 | NULL | +--------+-------+------+ ```

array_any_value.name: array_any_value
array_any_value.description: Returns the first non-null element in the array.

array_append.name: array_append
array_append.description: Appends an element to the end of an array.

array_dims.name: array_dims
array_dims.description: Returns an array of the array's dimensions.

array_distance.name: array_distance
array_distance.description: Returns the Euclidean distance between two input arrays of equal length.

array_distinct.name: array_distinct
array_distinct.description: Returns distinct values from the array after removing duplicates.

array_element.name: array_element
array_element.description: Extracts the element with the index n from the array.

array_except.name: array_except
array_except.description: Returns an array of the elements that appear in the first array but not in the second.

array_has.name: array_has
array_has.description: Returns true if the array contains the element.

array_has_all.name: array_has_all
array_has_all.description: Returns true if all elements of sub-array exist in array.

array_has_any.name: array_has_any
array_has_any.description: Returns true if any elements exist in both arrays.

array_intersect.name: array_intersect
array_intersect.description: Returns an array of elements in the intersection of array1 and array2.

array_length.name: array_length
array_length.description: Returns the length of the array dimension.

array_max.name: array_max
array_max.description: Returns the maximum value in the array.

array_min.name: array_min
array_min.description: Returns the minimum value in the array.

array_ndims.name: array_ndims
array_ndims.description: Returns the number of dimensions of the array.

array_pop_back.name: array_pop_back
array_pop_back.description: Returns the array without the last element.

array_pop_front.name: array_pop_front
array_pop_front.description: Returns the array without the first element.

array_position.name: array_position
array_position.description: Returns the position of the first occurrence of the specified element in the array, or NULL if not found.

array_positions.name: array_positions
array_positions.description: Searches for an element in the array, returns all occurrences.

array_prepend.name: array_prepend
array_prepend.description: Prepends an element to the beginning of an array.

array_remove.name: array_remove
array_remove.description: Removes the first element from the array equal to the given value.

array_remove_all.name: array_remove_all
array_remove_all.description: Removes all elements from the array equal to the given value.

array_remove_n.name: array_remove_n
array_remove_n.description: Removes the first `max` elements from the array equal to the given value.

array_repeat.name: array_repeat
array_repeat.description: Returns an array containing element `count` times.

array_replace.name: array_replace
array_replace.description: Replaces the first occurrence of the specified element with another specified element.

array_replace_all.name: array_replace_all
array_replace_all.description: Replaces all occurrences of the specified element with another specified element.

array_replace_n.name: array_replace_n
array_replace_n.description: Replaces the first `max` occurrences of the specified element with another specified element.

array_resize.name: array_resize
array_resize.description: Resizes the list to contain size elements. Initializes new elements with value or empty if value is not set.

array_reverse.name: array_reverse
array_reverse.description: Returns the array with the order of the elements reversed.

array_slice.name: array_slice
array_slice.description: Returns a slice of the array based on 1-indexed start and end positions.

array_to_string.name: array_to_string
array_to_string.description: Converts each element to its text representation.

array_union.name: array_union
array_union.description: Returns an array of elements that are present in both arrays (all elements from both arrays) without duplicates.

cardinality.name: cardinality
cardinality.description: Returns the total number of elements in the array.

empty.name: empty
empty.description: Returns 1 for an empty array or 0 for a non-empty array.

flatten.name: flatten
flatten.description: Converts an array of arrays to a flat array. - Applies to any depth of nested arrays - Does not change arrays that are already flat The flattened array contains all the elements from all source arrays.

generate_series.name: generate_series
generate_series.description: Similar to the range function, but it includes the upper bound.

make_array.name: make_array
make_array.description: Returns an array using the specified input expressions.

range.name: range
range.description: Returns an Arrow array between start and stop with step. The range start..end contains all values with start <= x < end. It is empty if start >= end. Step cannot be 0.

string_to_array.name: string_to_array
string_to_array.description: Splits a string into an array of substrings based on a delimiter. Any substrings matching the optional `null_str` argument are replaced with NULL.

decode.name: decode
decode.description: Decode binary data from textual representation in string.

encode.name: encode
encode.description: Encode binary data into a textual representation.

coalesce.name: coalesce
coalesce.description: Returns the first of its arguments that is not _null_. Returns _null_ if all arguments are _null_. This function is often used to substitute a default value for _null_ values.

greatest.name: greatest
greatest.description: Returns the greatest value in a list of expressions. Returns _null_ if all expressions are _null_.

least.name: least
least.description: Returns the smallest value in a list of expressions. Returns _null_ if all expressions are _null_.

nvl.name: nvl
nvl.description: Returns _expression2_ if _expression1_ is NULL otherwise it returns _expression1_ and _expression2_ is not evaluated. This function can be used to substitute a default value for NULL values.

nvl2.name: nvl2
nvl2.description: Returns _expression2_ if _expression1_ is not NULL; otherwise it returns _expression3_.

digest.name: digest
digest.description: Computes the binary hash of an expression using the specified algorithm.

md5.name: md5
md5.description: Computes an MD5 128-bit checksum for a string expression.

sha224.name: sha224
sha224.description: Computes the SHA-224 hash of a binary string.

sha256.name: sha256
sha256.description: Computes the SHA-256 hash of a binary string.

sha384.name: sha384
sha384.description: Computes the SHA-384 hash of a binary string.

sha512.name: sha512
sha512.description: Computes the SHA-512 hash of a binary string.

map.name: map
map.description: Returns an Arrow map with the specified key-value pairs. The `make_map` function creates a map from two lists: one for keys and one for values. Each key must be unique and non-null.

map_entries.name: map_entries
map_entries.description: Returns a list of all entries in the map.

map_extract.name: map_extract
map_extract.description: Returns a list containing the value for the given key or an empty list if the key is not present in the map.

map_keys.name: map_keys
map_keys.description: Returns a list of all keys in the map.

map_values.name: map_values
map_values.description: Returns a list of all values in the map.

abs.name: abs
abs.description: Returns the absolute value of a number.

acos.name: acos
acos.description: Returns the arc cosine or inverse cosine of a number.

acosh.name: acosh
acosh.description: Returns the area hyperbolic cosine or inverse hyperbolic cosine of a number.

asin.name: asin
asin.description: Returns the arc sine or inverse sine of a number.

asinh.name: asinh
asinh.description: Returns the area hyperbolic sine or inverse hyperbolic sine of a number.

atan.name: atan
atan.description: Returns the arc tangent or inverse tangent of a number.

atan2.name: atan2
atan2.description: Returns the arc tangent or inverse tangent of `expression_y / expression_x`.

atanh.name: atanh
atanh.description: Returns the area hyperbolic tangent or inverse hyperbolic tangent of a number.

cbrt.name: cbrt
cbrt.description: Returns the cube root of a number.

ceil.name: ceil
ceil.description: Returns the nearest integer greater than or equal to a number.

cos.name: cos
cos.description: Returns the cosine of a number.

cosh.name: cosh
cosh.description: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of a number.

cot.name: cot
cot.description: Returns the cotangent of a number.

exp.name: exp
exp.description: Returns the base-e exponential of a number.

factorial.name: factorial
factorial.description: Factorial. Returns 1 if value is less than 2.

floor.name: floor
floor.description: Returns the nearest integer less than or equal to a number.

gcd.name: gcd
gcd.description: Returns the greatest common divisor of `expression_x` and `expression_y`. Returns 0 if both inputs are zero.

isnan.name: isnan
isnan.description: Returns true if a given number is +NaN or -NaN otherwise returns false.

iszero.name: iszero
iszero.description: Returns true if a given number is +0.0 or -0.0 otherwise returns false.

lcm.name: lcm
lcm.description: Returns the least common multiple of `expression_x` and `expression_y`. Returns 0 if either input is zero.

ln.name: ln
ln.description: Returns the natural logarithm of a number.

log.name: log
log.description: Returns the base-x logarithm of a number. Can either provide a specified base, or if omitted then takes the base-10 of a number.

log10.name: log10
log10.description: Returns the base-10 logarithm of a number.

log2.name: log2
log2.description: Returns the base-2 logarithm of a number.

nanvl.name: nanvl
nanvl.description: Returns the first argument if it's not _NaN_. Returns the second argument otherwise.

pi.name: pi
pi.description: Returns an approximate value of π.

power.name: power
power.description: Returns a base expression raised to the power of an exponent.

random.name: random
random.description: Returns a random float value in the range [0, 1). The random seed is unique to each row.

round.name: round
round.description: Rounds a number to the nearest integer.

signum.name: signum
signum.description: Returns the sign of a number. Negative numbers return `-1`. Zero and positive numbers return `1`.

sin.name: sin
sin.description: Returns the sine of a number.

sinh.name: sinh
sinh.description: Returns the hyperbolic sine of a number.

sqrt.name: sqrt
sqrt.description: Returns the square root of a number.

tan.name: tan
tan.description: Returns the tangent of a number.

tanh.name: tanh
tanh.description: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of a number.

trunc.name: trunc
trunc.description: Truncates a number to a whole number or truncated to the specified decimal places.

arrow_cast.name: arrow_cast
arrow_cast.description: Casts a value to a specific Arrow data type.
arrow_cast.example:
select
 arrow_cast(-5, 'Int8') as a,
 arrow_cast('foo', 'Dictionary(Int32, Utf8)') as b,
 arrow_cast('bar', 'LargeUtf8') as c;

arrow_metadata.name: arrow_metadata
arrow_metadata.description: Returns the metadata of the input expression. If a key is provided, returns the value for that key. If no key is provided, returns a Map of all metadata.

arrow_typeof.name: arrow_typeof
arrow_typeof.description: Returns the name of the underlying [Arrow data type](https://docs.rs/arrow/latest/arrow/datatypes/enum.DataType.html) of the expression.

get_field.name: get_field
get_field.description: Returns a field within a map or a struct with the given key. Supports nested field access by providing multiple field names. Note: most users invoke `get_field` indirectly via field access syntax such as `my_struct_col['field_name']` which results in a call to `get_field(my_struct_col, 'field_name')`. Nested access like `my_struct['a']['b']` is optimized to a single call: `get_field(my_struct, 'a', 'b')`.

regexp_instr.name: regexp_instr
regexp_instr.description: Returns the position in a string where the specified occurrence of a POSIX regular expression is located.
regexp_instr.syntax: regexp_instr(str, regexp[, start[, N[, flags[, subexpr]]]])

ascii.name: ascii
ascii.description: Returns the first Unicode scalar value of a string.

bit_length.name: bit_length
bit_length.description: Returns the bit length of a string.

btrim.name: btrim
btrim.description: Trims the specified trim string from the start and end of a string. If no trim string is provided, all whitespace is removed from the start and end of the input string.

character_length.name: character_length
character_length.description: Returns the number of characters in a string.

chr.name: chr
chr.description: Returns a string containing the character with the specified Unicode scalar value.

concat_ws.name: concat_ws
concat_ws.description: Concatenates multiple strings together with a specified separator.

contains.name: contains
contains.description: Return true if search_str is found within string (case-sensitive).

ends_with.name: ends_with
ends_with.description: Tests if a string ends with a substring.

find_in_set.name: find_in_set
find_in_set.description: Returns a value in the range of 1 to N if the string str is in the string list strlist consisting of N substrings.

initcap.name: initcap
initcap.description: Capitalizes the first character in each word in the input string. Words are delimited by non-alphanumeric characters.

left.name: left
left.description: Returns a specified number of characters from the left side of a string.

levenshtein.name: levenshtein
levenshtein.description: Returns the [`Levenshtein distance`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levenshtein_distance) between the two given strings.

lpad.name: lpad
lpad.description: Pads the left side of a string with another string to a specified string length.

ltrim.name: ltrim
ltrim.description: Trims the specified trim string from the beginning of a string. If no trim string is provided, all whitespace is removed from the start of the input string.

octet_length.name: octet_length
octet_length.description: Returns the length of a string in bytes.

overlay.name: overlay
overlay.description: Returns the string which is replaced by another string from the specified position and specified count length.
overlay.syntax: overlay(str PLACING substr FROM pos [FOR count])

repeat.name: repeat
repeat.description: Returns a string with an input string repeated a specified number.

replace.name: replace
replace.description: Replaces all occurrences of a specified substring in a string with a new substring.

reverse.name: reverse
reverse.description: Reverses the character order of a string.

right.name: right
right.description: Returns a specified number of characters from the right side of a string.

rpad.name: rpad
rpad.description: Pads the right side of a string with another string to a specified string length.

rtrim.name: rtrim
rtrim.description: Trims the specified trim string from the end of a string. If no trim string is provided, all whitespace is removed from the end of the input string.

split_part.name: split_part
split_part.description: Splits a string based on a specified delimiter and returns the substring in the specified position.

starts_with.name: starts_with
starts_with.description: Tests if a string starts with a substring.

strpos.name: strpos
strpos.description: Returns the starting position of a specified substring in a string. Positions begin at 1. If the substring does not exist in the string, the function returns 0.

substr.name: substr
substr.description: Extracts a substring of a specified number of characters from a specific starting position in a string.

substr_index.name: substr_index
substr_index.description: Returns the substring from str before count occurrences of the delimiter delim. If count is positive, everything to the left of the final delimiter (counting from the left) is returned. If count is negative, everything to the right of the final delimiter (counting from the right) is returned.

to_hex.name: to_hex
to_hex.description: Converts an integer to a hexadecimal string.

translate.name: translate
translate.description: Translates characters in a string to specified translation characters.

named_struct.name: named_struct
named_struct.description: Returns an Arrow struct using the specified name and input expressions pairs.

struct.name: struct
struct.description: Returns an Arrow struct using the specified input expressions optionally named. Fields in the returned struct use the optional name or the `cN` naming convention. For example: `c0`, `c1`, `c2`, etc.

current_date.name: current_date
current_date.description: Returns the current date in the session time zone. The `current_date()` return value is determined at query time and will return the same date, no matter when in the query plan the function executes.

current_time.name: current_time
current_time.description: Returns the current time in the session time zone. The `current_time()` return value is determined at query time and will return the same time, no matter when in the query plan the function executes. The session time zone can be set using the statement 'SET datafusion.execution.time_zone = desired time zone'. The time zone can be a value like +00:00, 'Europe/London' etc.

date_bin.name: date_bin
date_bin.description: Calculates time intervals and returns the start of the interval nearest to the specified timestamp. Use `date_bin` to downsample time series data by grouping rows into time-based "bins" or "windows" and applying an aggregate or selector function to each window. For example, if you "bin" or "window" data into 15 minute intervals, an input timestamp of `2023-01-01T18:18:18Z` will be updated to the start time of the 15 minute bin it is in: `2023-01-01T18:15:00Z`.
date_bin.example:
SELECT date_bin(interval '1 day', time) as bin
FROM VALUES ('2023-01-01T18:18:18Z'), ('2023-01-03T19:00:03Z') t(time);

date_part.name: date_part
date_part.description: Returns the specified part of the date as an integer.

date_trunc.name: date_trunc
date_trunc.description: Truncates a timestamp or time value to a specified precision.

from_unixtime.name: from_unixtime
from_unixtime.description: Converts an integer to RFC3339 timestamp format (`YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.000000000Z`). Integers and unsigned integers are interpreted as seconds since the unix epoch (`1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`) return the corresponding timestamp.

make_date.name: make_date
make_date.description: Make a date from year/month/day component parts.

make_time.name: make_time
make_time.description: Make a time from hour/minute/second component parts.

now.name: now
now.description: Returns the current timestamp in the system configured timezone (None by default). The `now()` return value is determined at query time and will return the same timestamp, no matter when in the query plan the function executes.

to_char.name: to_char
to_char.description: Returns a string representation of a date, time, timestamp or duration based on a [Chrono format](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/format/strftime/index.html). Unlike the PostgreSQL equivalent of this function numerical formatting is not supported.

to_date.name: to_date
to_date.description: Converts a value to a date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Supports strings, numeric and timestamp types as input. Strings are parsed as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. '2023-07-20') if no [Chrono format](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/format/strftime/index.html)s are provided. Integers and doubles are interpreted as days since the unix epoch (`1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`). Returns the corresponding date. Note: `to_date` returns Date32, which represents its values as the number of days since unix epoch(`1970-01-01`) stored as

to_local_time.name: to_local_time
to_local_time.description: Converts a timestamp with a timezone to a timestamp without a timezone (with no offset or timezone information). This function handles daylight saving time changes.

to_time.name: to_time
to_time.description: Converts a value to a time (`HH:MM:SS.nnnnnnnnn`). Supports strings and timestamps as input. Strings are parsed as `HH:MM:SS`, `HH:MM:SS.nnnnnnnnn`, or `HH:MM` if no [Chrono format](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/format/strftime/index.html)s are provided. Timestamps will have the time portion extracted. Returns the corresponding time. Note: `to_time` returns Time64(Nanosecond), which represents the time of day in nanoseconds since midnight.

to_timestamp.name: to_timestamp
to_timestamp.description: Converts a value to a timestamp (`YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.000000<TZ>`) in the session time zone. Supports strings, integer, unsigned integer, and double types as input. Strings are parsed as RFC3339 (e.g. '2023-07-20T05:44:00') if no [Chrono formats](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/format/strftime/index.html) are provided. Strings that parse without a time zone are treated as if they are in the session time zone, or UTC if no session time zone is set. Integers, unsigned integers, and doubles ar

to_timestamp_micros.name: to_timestamp_micros
to_timestamp_micros.description: Converts a value to a timestamp (`YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.000000<TZ>`) in the session time zone. Supports strings, integer, unsigned integer, and double types as input. Strings are parsed as RFC3339 (e.g. '2023-07-20T05:44:00') if no [Chrono formats](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/format/strftime/index.html) are provided. Strings that parse without a time zone are treated as if they are in the session time zone, or UTC if no session time zone is set. Integers, unsigned integers, and doubles ar

to_timestamp_millis.name: to_timestamp_millis
to_timestamp_millis.description: Converts a value to a timestamp (`YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.000<TZ>`) in the session time zone. Supports strings, integer, unsigned integer, and double types as input. to_unixtime.name: to_unixtime
to_unixtime.description: Converts a value to seconds since the unix epoch (`1970-01-01T00:00:00`). Supports strings, dates, timestamps, integer, unsigned integer, and float types as input. Strings are parsed as RFC3339 (e.g. '2023-07-20T05:44:00') if no [Chrono formats](https://docs.rs/chrono/latest/chrono/format/strftime/index.html) are provided. Integers, unsigned integers, and floats are interpreted as seconds since the unix epoch (`1970-01-01T00:00:00`).

union_extract.name: union_extract
union_extract.description: Returns the value of the given field in the union when selected, or NULL otherwise.
union_extract.example: select union_column, union_extract(union_column, 'a'), union_extract(union_column, 'b') from table_with_union;

union_tag.name: union_tag
union_tag.description: Returns the name of the currently selected field in the union

unnest.name: unnest
unnest.description: Expands an array or map into rows.

example.name: example
example.description: ```sql SELECT column_1, ( SELECT first_value(string) FROM y WHERE number = x.column_1 ) AS "numeric string" FROM x; +----------+----------------+ | column_1 | numeric string | +----------+----------------+ | 1 | one | | 2 | two | +----------+----------------+ ```

examples.name: examples
examples.description: The following query calculates the averages of even and odd numbers in table `y` and returns the averages that are equal to the maximum value of `column_1` in table `x`.

lag.name: lag
lag.description: Returns value evaluated at the row that is offset rows before the current row within the partition; if there is no such row, instead return default (which must be of the same type as value).
lag.example:
SELECT employee_id,
 salary,
 lag(salary, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY employee_id) AS prev_salary
FROM employees;

lead.name: lead
lead.description: Returns value evaluated at the row that is offset rows after the current row within the partition; if there is no such row, instead return default (which must be of the same type as value).
lead.example:
SELECT
 employee_id,
 department,
 salary,
 lead(salary, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary) AS next_salary
FROM employees;

cume_dist.name: cume_dist
cume_dist.description: Relative rank of the current row: (number of rows preceding or peer with the current row) / (total rows).

dense_rank.name: dense_rank
dense_rank.description: Returns the rank of the current row without gaps. This function ranks rows in a dense manner, meaning consecutive ranks are assigned even for identical values.
dense_rank.example:
SELECT department,
 salary,
 dense_rank() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS dense_rank
FROM employees;

ntile.name: ntile
ntile.description: Integer ranging from 1 to the argument value, dividing the partition as equally as possible
ntile.example:
SELECT employee_id,
 salary,
 ntile(4) OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS quartile
FROM employees;

percent_rank.name: percent_rank
percent_rank.description: Returns the percentage rank of the current row within its partition. The value ranges from 0 to 1 and is computed as `(rank - 1) / (total_rows - 1)`.
percent_rank.example:
SELECT employee_id,
 salary,
 percent_rank() OVER (ORDER BY salary) AS percent_rank
FROM employees;

rank.name: rank
rank.description: Returns the rank of the current row within its partition, allowing gaps between ranks. This function provides a ranking similar to `row_number`, but skips ranks for identical values.
rank.example:
SELECT department,
 salary,
 rank() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rank
FROM employees;

row_number.name: row_number
row_number.description: Number of the current row within its partition, counting from 1.
row_number.example:
SELECT department,
 salary,
 row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS row_num
FROM employees;

str_match.name: str_match
str_match.description: filter the keyword in the field.

str_match_ignore_case.name: str_match_ignore_case
str_match_ignore_case.description: filter the keyword in the field with case_insensitive. it can match `KeyWord` or `keyWord`.

match_all.name: match_all
match_all.description: filter the keyword in the fields, whose **Index Type** is set to `Full text search` in streams settings.

match_all_raw.name: match_all_raw
match_all_raw.description: filter the keyword in multiple fields. Unlike `match_all`, `match_all_raw` does not utilize `Inverted Index`, instead searches through entire original data. This function is case-sensitive.

re_match.name: re_match
re_match.description: use regexp to match the pattern in the field. Please refer to [Regex](https://docs.rs/regex/latest/regex/) for Regex Syntax.

re_not_match.name: re_not_match
re_not_match.description: use regexp to not match the pattern in the field.

arr_descending.name: arr_descending
arr_descending.description: Sorts the given array field in descending order. E.g. `arr_descending(arrfield)`. Expects the array fields to be of same type.
arr_descending.example: SELECT *, arr_descending(numbers) as descending_numbers FROM "default" ORDER BY _timestamp DESC

arrcount.name: arrcount
arrcount.description: Counts elements in an array. E.g. `arrcount(arrfield)` returns the number of elements in the array field.
arrcount.example: SELECT *, arrcount(numbers) as number_count FROM "default" ORDER BY _timestamp DESC

arrindex.name: arrindex
arrindex.description: Selects a range of elements from an array. arrindex(field, start, end) where end is inclusive. E.g. `arrindex(arrfield, 0, 0)` returns `"[\"element1\"]"`.
arrindex.example: SELECT *, arrindex(elements, 0, 2) as three_elements FROM "default" ORDER BY _timestamp DESC

arrjoin.name: arrjoin
arrjoin.description: Concatenates arrays with a specified delimiter. E.g. arrjoin(field, ' | ') returns "element1 | element2 | element3".
arrjoin.example: SELECT *, arrjoin(numbers, ' | ') as joined_numbers FROM "default" ORDER BY _timestamp DESC

arrsort.name: arrsort
arrsort.description: Sorts the array field in increasing order. E.g. `arrsort(arrfield)`. Expects the array field elements to be of same type (e.g. array of numbers).
arrsort.example: SELECT *, arrsort(numbers) as increasing_numbers FROM "default" ORDER BY _timestamp DESC

arrzip.name: arrzip
arrzip.description: Zips multiple array fields together with a delimiter. E.g. `arrzip(arrfield1, arrfield2, ',')` returns "[\"element01,element11\", \"element02,element12\"]".
arrzip.example: SELECT *, arrzip(numbers, strings, '|') as zipped_field FROM "default" ORDER BY _timestamp DESC

spath.name: spath
spath.description: Works on Json object by splitting paths and extracting values. E.g - Say we have a field `json_object_field` which contains value like - `"{\"nested\": {\"value\": 23}}"`. We can extract the value of `nested.value` with this - `spath(json_object_field, 'nested.value')`.
spath.example: SELECT *, spath(json_object_field, 'nested.value') as nested_value FROM "default" ORDER BY _timestamp DESC

cast_to_arr.name: cast_to_arr
cast_to_arr.description: Casts an json array string to a native datafusion array that can be used with `unnest(cast_to_arr(field))`, and other datafusion array functions such as `array_pop_back(cast_to_arr(arrfield))` etc.
cast_to_arr.example: SELECT _timestamp, bools, games, nums, floats, less, arrzip(bools, games, ' | ') as zipped_bools_games, arrindex(nums, 0, 0) as num_index, array_union(cast_to_arr(nums), cast_to_arr(less)) as union_nums_less, arrjoin(nums, ',') as joined_nums FROM "arr_udf" ORDER BY _timestamp DESC

to_array_string.name: to_array_string
to_array_string.description: It is a reverse of `cast_to_arr(field)` to improve the interoperability between stringified json array fields in openobserve streams and native datafusion arrays.
to_array_string.example: SELECT *, arrsort(to_array_string(array_concat(cast_to_arr(numbers), cast_to_arr(more_numbers)))) as increasing_numbers FROM "default" ORDER BY _timestamp DESC

histogram.name: histogram
histogram.description: Creates time-based histogram buckets for aggregation. Supports interval strings (e.g., '30 seconds', 'hour') or number of buckets.
histogram.example: SELECT histogram(_timestamp, '30 seconds') AS key, COUNT(*) AS num FROM stream GROUP BY key ORDER BY key

aggregate.description: Functions that operate on sets of values to compute a single result

scalar.description: Functions that operate on single values and return a single value

window.description: Functions for window/analytic operations over partitions
